Q_rationally_soluble_hence_all_places.witness_d2: x=q, y=q(q+1); A=2q^2 and B=2q^2(q+1)^2, so the d=2 split-cover equations have a rational point. This x=q point is a Face-3 pole/order-4 torsion point and gives local-solubility credit only, not receiver survival.

Q7_insoluble.proof: For these eight classes d is a 7-adic unit. Normalize a hypothetical Q_7 point so X,Z are integral and not both divisible by 7. The three integral square equations reduce to P^1(F_7). Exhaustion of all eight projective residues finds none satisfying E_h square, A_h/d square and B_h/d square simultaneously.
